correctness.rationale: For u=t+2 and x=tu, the right-hand side is t²u²(4tu+3u²+3t²)=2t²u² in characteristic five. The discriminant is t³u⁴ and j=4u⁵. The local discriminant orders in the minimal coordinates are 3,4,5 at 0,3,infinity (at infinity rescale by s² and s³), with types III, IV and I5 as in the original paper. P reduces to the singular point in each minimal Weierstrass fiber, respectively (0,0),(0,0),(1,0), and is disjoint from O. The identity component of the smooth model is the smooth locus of the Weierstrass fiber; sections of the regular model meet the smooth part of the fibration, so these reductions force nonidentity components, not a point of intersection on the strict transform. Their contributions are 1/2, 2/3 and either 4/5 or 6/5. The rational surface has chi=1, so the latter option gives a negative height -11/30; the former gives 1/30. The unimodular rank-ten NS lattice and root ranks 1+2+4 force geometric rank one, and the trivial-lattice determinant is 30. For a primitive free generator G its self-pairing is |T|²/30, T the finite torsion. Writing P=nG modulo torsion yields n²|T|²=1, proving both primitivity and torsion-freeness. Frobenius acts on alpha by alpha^5=-alpha and on P by negation, so its m-th invariants give the exact constant-field groups. The quadratic twist isomorphism (x,Y)↦(x,alpha Y) changes the descent sign and identifies the stated primitive generator.
residual_risks: No formal certificate; the checker verifies algebraic identities only. Conclusions are only for constant-field extensions, not arbitrary extensions of the function field.

evidence: The e5ffefd1cc57 resolved-fiber counts (11,3,4,6,5,7) sum to 36. The normalized Frobenius trace on NS is (36−1−25)/5=2. The trivial lattice trace is 3: O, the fiber and the III component are fixed; IV exchanges two nonidentity components (nonsquare tangent), and nonsplit I5 reverses its cycle, pairing the four nonidentity components. Hence the rank-one quotient has trace −1.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Thus known point-count data for the nearby indexed object already imply the abstract parity of the rank (and, with torsion-freeness, the abstract groups). These data do not yield a primitive coordinate section. In the older twist equation one can reconstruct the specific section by exploiting all three singular reductions, degree bounds from disjointness with O, and a final coefficient check; the earlier example does not perform that reconstruction or the local height/index verification. This is a supported generator-level result, not novelty for the equations, lattice type, or Frobenius sign in isolation.
